results.note: The require_exactly_one_frozen_declaration validator rejects an entry that declares both or neither. Tests at test_registry.py:138 (neither) and :148 (both) cover it, and the pytest gate exits 0.

derives_from was added at line 121, and any talib_function entry without it is rejected at line 184. The test at test_registry.py:165 covers this. The field is required, but the shipped values are wrong (see C6).
reject_unknown_derived_roots rejects keys that don't exist, and the test at :173 covers it. It does not reject self-references (x derives_from x), which is how C6 slipped through.
freshness_unmeasurable: NonEmptyString | None was added to IndicatorDefinition.

The test loads the shipped registry and checks three things: every entry has exactly one declaration, btc_daily_close has frozen_after_observations, and all four funding entries have expected_constant with a reason mentioning '0.01%' and 'clamp'.

Only BTC's links are correct (they point at btc_daily_close). eth_rsi, sol_rsi and bnb_rsi each point at themselves (registry.yaml:381, :724, :1051), and every ETH/SOL/BNB EMA/ATR/BBANDS/OBV/MACD/StochRSI entry points at that asset's RSI instead of its underlying price/volume series. The spec asks for 'the correct underlying price/volume series for its own asset'. The test only checks that the key exists (`entry.derives_from in entries`), so it passes even with these self-loops. Downstream frozen propagation (US-1004) would never catch a frozen ETH/SOL/BNB close through these links.

stablecoin_supply (registry.yaml ~1512) and sol_staking (~784) both declare freshness_unmeasurable. The reasons say source_timestamp comes from fetched_at or the fetch wall clock, and the test asserts on that content.
load_registry raises ValidationError at load time when the frozen declaration is missing (:138) or derives_from is missing (:165). assert_registry_coverage was also extended (registry.py:376-383).

note: The schema, validators and most of the data are real, but C6 fails. For ETH, SOL and BNB, derives_from forms self-loops (eth_rsi→eth_rsi, etc.) and the other TA-Lib entries point at RSI instead of a price/volume root. The C6 test only checks that the key exists, so it doesn't actually check that the links are correct.
